subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle contract for subagent startup, and should the stale open PR be replaced with a current-main implementation?
rationale: The source-repro is strong, but the repair changes a core lifecycle/API surface used by agents, gateway projections, session state, and SDK consumers, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Approve Current-Main Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Sponsor a fresh or adopted implementation that wires the new phases through active embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway/session, SDK, docs, and focused proof.

options.title: Narrow To Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep the existing phase contract and require a smaller fix that improves logs/timeouts without adding new lifecycle phases.

options.title: Decline Core Event Surface
options.body: Close or defer the lifecycle phase request and keep any specialized startup watchdog behavior outside the core contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Current-Main Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a fresh or adopted implementation that wires the new phases through active embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway/session, SDK, docs, and focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is prior subagent lifecycle stabilization and registry lifecycle ownership on the files that would define the durable contract.
